key_insight: AeroZoo shows that explicit boundary-condition inputs sharply improve aerodynamic flow prediction, while unseen enclosures and boundary-condition layouts remain major generalization challenges.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark tests whether fast CFD surrogates can handle new shapes and flow domains using solver-style inputs rather than geometry alone.
method: Generate 3,815 time-mean unsteady RANS solutions with a transition model across seven geometry families, eight enclosures and Reynolds numbers from 10³ to 10⁸.
Specify each problem through boundary meshes grouped by condition type, prescribed values and fluid properties.
Evaluate two tasks using engineering metrics and 22 frozen, geometry-disjoint splits.
evidence_signal: On the 2,816-sample canonical benchmark's random split, boundary-condition tokens reduced GeoTransolver's median velocity error from 76.9% to 8.4% of inlet speed in single-seed runs; ISLA reached 5.3% over four seeds.
watch_item: Held-out enclosures or boundary-condition layouts increased ISLA's error by 2.4–9.2×, cautioning against assuming reliable deployment beyond training conditions.
paper_title: AeroZoo: A Benchmark of Well-Posed Flow Problems for Foundation Models of Aerodynamics
